metadata.disclaimer: Based on NIST SP 800-171 Rev 3 (May 2024). NIST derived each of its security requirements from named SP 800-53 Rev 5 controls, its source controls. Federal agencies apply SP 800-171 to nonfederal organizations through contracts and other agreements. It protects the confidentiality of Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) in the system components that process, store or transmit CUI, and in the components that protect them. Where a requirement has an organization-defined parameter, use the value the agency sets in the contract, if it sets one. Clause ids and titles are NIST's. Validate with qualified assessors for compliance or audit use.
metadata.clause_titles_from: NIST SP 800-171 Rev 3, Protecting Controlled Unclassified Information in Nonfederal Systems and Organizations (May 2024), as in NIST's Cybersecurity and Privacy Reference Tool

crosswalk_check.source: NIST, SP 800-171 Rev 3 (May 2024), the source controls of each requirement, from the 800-171r3 dataset in NIST's Cybersecurity and Privacy Reference Tool (CPRT), version 3.0.0
crosswalk_check.scope: Base controls only. NIST lists the SP 800-53 controls behind each requirement as its source controls. They are the base of this mapping, and every one is here. NIST's 157 source controls give 123 pairs of a requirement and a base control. A source control that is an enhancement, such as AC-02(03), counts for its base control, AC-02, as in the HIPAA and NERC CIP mappings. Of the 123 pairs, 9 come from enhancements alone. source_controls keeps NIST's own list for each requirement. NIST names the controls of SP 800-53 Release 5.1.1, and each one is current in Release 5.2.0, so every pair stays. Every pair is NIST's, so not_in_source is empty. The clauses are the 97 active requirements, in NIST's order. Rev 3 withdrew 33 more, listed under withdrawn_requirements with NIST's reasons. The coverage figures, rationales and gaps are OSA's, written on 2026-11-01 for these pairs. A requirement has 95, OSA's highest figure, where implementing its source controls as NIST states them meets it. The 5 that ask for something more have 90, and their gaps say what.
crosswalk_check.compared_with: The source controls in the CPRT export match those printed in the publication (NIST.SP.800-171r3.pdf, sha256 3e4631df8b5d61f40a6e542b52779ef30ddbbfff31e09214fa94ad6e6f5e6d08) for all 97 requirements. NIST's CUI Overlay (sp800-171r3-cui-overlay.xlsx, sha256 c69914ac7d364b3ec6b661474102389072b5a293bc2dca156433dedd2d1e6da7) places the same controls on 92 of them. For two of the other five, the overlay's sort ids for IA-06 and SI-05 read IA-06-06 and SI-05-05, and the controls agree once those are read as IA-06 and SI-05. The overlay places AU-09(04) on 03.03.08 and SC-28 on 03.13.08, where the publication also names them for 03.01.05 and 03.08.05. It also places AC-17(02) on 03.13.08, which the publication leaves out there. This mapping follows the publication, so 03.13.08 has SC-08 and SC-28.
